hints: At constant speed on horizontal ground, the forward driving force equals the resistance force: $F_D = F_{\text{res}}$.
Use $P = F_D \times v$, converting $16\text{ kW}$ to $16000\text{ W}$ at $v = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Solve $16000 = F \times 40$ for the resistance force $F = 400\text{ N}$.
walkthrough:
State the formula for instantaneous power developed by an engine:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Convert the engine power from kilowatts to watts:
$$P = 16\text{ kW} = 16 \times 1000 = 16000\text{ W}$$

Because the car travels at constant speed on a level road, the resultant horizontal force is zero ($a = 0$), which means the driving force equals the resistance force:
$$F_D = F_{\text{res}}$$

Substitute $P = 16000\text{ W}$ and $v = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$ into the power formula:
$$16000 = F_{\text{res}} \times 40$$

Divide both sides by $40$ to find the resistance force:
$$F_{\text{res}} = \frac{16000}{40} = 400\text{ N}$$

hints: Find the driving force at speed $45\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with increased power $22.5\text{ kW} = 22500\text{ W}$: $F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{22500}{45}$.
Apply Newton's second law horizontally: $F_D - F_{\text{res}} = ma$, using the constant resistance $F_{\text{res}} = 400\text{ N}$ from part (i)(a) and mass $m = 1200\text{ kg}$.
walkthrough:
Convert the new power to watts:
$$P = 22.5\text{ kW} = 22500\text{ W}$$

Determine the driving force exerted by the engine at the instant speed is $v = 45\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{22500}{45} = 500\text{ N}$$

State Newton's second law along the horizontal direction of motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma \implies F_D - F_{\text{res}} = ma$$

Substitute driving force $F_D = 500\text{ N}$, constant resistance $F_{\text{res}} = 400\text{ N}$, and mass $m = 1200\text{ kg}$:
$$500 - 400 = 1200a$$
$$100 = 1200a$$

Divide both sides by $1200$ to isolate $a$:
$$a = \frac{100}{1200} = \frac{1}{12}\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Convert to a decimal rounded to 3 significant figures:
$$a = \frac{1}{12} \approx 0.083333\text{ m s}^{-2} = 0.0833\text{ m s}^{-2} \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$

hints: At constant speed on a horizontal road, driving force equals resistance: $F_D = 590 + 2v$.
Use power $P = F_D \times v$, converting $16\text{ kW} = 16000\text{ W}$: $16000 = (590 + 2v)v$.
Expand and rearrange into a quadratic equation: $2v^2 + 590v - 16000 = 0 \implies v^2 + 295v - 8000 = 0$.
Factorise $(v - 25)(v + 320) = 0$ or use the quadratic formula to find the positive speed $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
State the power formula relating driving force and velocity:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Because the car travels at constant speed on horizontal ground, acceleration is zero, so the driving force equals the velocity-dependent resistance:
$$F_D = F_{\text{res}} = 590 + 2v$$

Convert the power to watts ($16\text{ kW} = 16000\text{ W}$) and substitute $F_D$:
$$16000 = (590 + 2v)v$$

Rearrange to form a standard quadratic equation set to zero:
$$2v^2 + 590v - 16000 = 0$$

Solve for $v$ using the quadratic formula $v = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$:
$$v = \frac{-295 \pm \sqrt{295^2 - 4(1)(-8000)}}{2} = \frac{-295 \pm \sqrt{87025 + 32000}}{2} = \frac{-295 \pm \sqrt{119025}}{2}$$
$$\sqrt{119025} = 345 \implies v = \frac{-295 + 345}{2} = \frac{50}{2} = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
